phase: One defect, two faces — Face A (swap-teleport re-anchor) already applied in working tree and kept; Face B (rebase/reset frame-shift during HYPER) is the new work. Re-anchor mechanism chosen at implementation per Max greenlight.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A coordinate-frame shift (a worldOrigin delta from rebase OR resetWorldOrigin) applied while warp is active leaves the tunnel pinned to the camera — the tunnel's camera-relative position is preserved, it does not orphan.

verifyVia.input: In a headless test (sibling to orbit-ring-rebase.test.js), put the warp into an active/HYPER state with the tunnel anchored at the camera, then simulate a worldOrigin shift of magnitude D (both a maybeRebase-style shift and a resetWorldOrigin-style zeroing).
verifyVia.observable: After the shift, the tunnel's position relative to the camera is unchanged (camera-relative offset within epsilon of pre-shift); absolute separation does NOT grow by ~D.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A second consecutive warp in the same session reaches portal mode INSIDE during HYPER with the tunnel mesh live at the camera (the Face-A path that used to lose to the fallback timer).

verifyVia.input: Run window.__wd.runRepeatWarpSuite() — two consecutive warps via _beginWarpTurn (RW1 clean baseline, RW2 precondition present, RW3 regression gate).
verifyVia.observable: On the repeat warp, portal mode reaches INSIDE during HYPER (insideAt non-null) and takeSceneInventory().meshes[name=='effect.warp.tunnel'].cameraDistance stays small (tunnel at camera, inFrustum), not orphaned.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A warp whose target triggers a rebase or resetWorldOrigin DURING HYPER still renders — the tunnel stays pinned to the camera through the frame shift instead of being left ~2800u behind.

verifyVia.input: Drive a warp to a far-enough target that a worldOrigin change fires during the INSIDE/HYPER window (sample tunnel cameraDistance / inFrustum / portal mode / worldOrigin per HYPER frame, per the prior session's ad-hoc probe pattern).
verifyVia.observable: tunnel cameraDistance stays small across the whole HYPER window even on the frame(s) where worldOrigin changes; it never jumps to ~teleport-distance and the tunnel never leaves the frustum → no black HYPER.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Because the defect is RNG-intermittent, the repeat-warp suite passes green RELIABLY across many consecutive runs, not just once.

verifyVia.input: Run runRepeatWarpSuite (and/or a multi-warp loop across varied seeds/targets) N times consecutively (N>=8), re-entering via window._lab.enterSol() between HMR reloads as needed.
verifyVia.observable: Every run reports the tunnel rendering during HYPER; zero black-HYPER occurrences across all N runs (the gate is multi-run, not single-pass).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The clean single warp from Sol still renders the tunnel, and the post-arrival fly-back portal follow and warp-landing-strip behavior are unchanged.

verifyVia.input: Run a single clean warp from Sol; then let the arrival fly-back play out; observe the OUTSIDE_B portal reposition (main.js:6782) and the warp-landing-strip.
verifyVia.observable: Single warp renders the tunnel during HYPER (RW1 baseline green); the fly-back portal still follows in OUTSIDE_B; the landing strip still persists/behaves as before — no new console errors.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max warps repeatedly around the galaxy — repeat warps and far targets — and never hits a black HYPER; warping feels reliable as a whole.

verifyVia.input: Max plays the running game and performs a series of warps (several repeats in one session, plus jumps to distant targets), watching the HYPER phase each time.
verifyVia.observable: Every warp shows the tunnel during HYPER; no black frames; the travel loop feels dependable. Holistic acceptance — deferred to Max.
